newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks bounce back on tariff news.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks bounce back on tariff news.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed sharply higher across the board in heavy trade Friday as market confidence recovered with the news of imminent tariff rises for market leaders, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index jumped 4.79 percent to 6,390.78 as 39 stocks rose, five fell and three closed flat.

"There was enthusiasm as confidence returned," said Ricardo Larrazabal of the Bancaracas brokerage. News that phone company CANTV and Electricidad de Caracas would receive tariff increases had boosted the market, he said.
"CANTV was the main news of the day which boosted confidence among investors in a much more enthusiastic market," Larrazabal said.
News that the Transport and Communications Ministry had approved CANTV's second quarter 4.18 percent rate increase outshone market concerns about a strike by CANTV workers which started Thursday.
CANTV stock rose 135.00 bolivars to 2,110.00 bolivars. The composite Merinvest index that includes CANTV rose 5.19 percent to 99.87.
A total of 9.597 billion bolivars ($20 million) changed hands in 1,015 trades.
Stocks had been oversold on a wave of recent market rumors and concerns over tariff rises and there was still room for prices to continue rising next week, brokers said.
Among heavily traded stocks, Electricidad de Caracas rose 21.00 bolivars to 515.00 bolivars, and steel company Sivensa rose 11.75 bolivars to 155.00 bolivars.
